haiku_trial.reason: Both inventories received the same packet and the same 14 lanes. Sonnet's 14 in_agents/in_workflows/in_hooks classifications all hold against source as it stood when it read (the QMD and prompt-caching rows are stale only because the files were rewritten at 18:19, after extraction); its defect is a systematic citation slip - it repeatedly cites evidence-reviewer.md:6 for the tools list, which is actually line 4 (line 5 is model, line 6 is effort). Haiku got five rows materially wrong: (1) RTK in_agents 'no' - isolated-builder.md:9 says 'keep RTK-filtered output and preserve raw-output recovery paths'; (2) Context Mode in_workflows 'no' - both PACKETs say 'Context Mode ctx_execute for large outputs' (review-changes.js:22, readiness-audit.js:25), and Haiku itself cites the PACKET for other lanes; (3) prompt-caching in_workflows 'no' with evidence that pairs a post-fix comment (review-changes.js:17) with the pre-fix divergence, a state that cannot have coexisted per git diff; (4) ToolSearch in_agents 'partial' on a fabricated attribution - it quotes 'load a schema with ToolSearch when it is deferred' as evidence-reviewer.md:9, but that string appears only in the workflow PACKET, and its second cite 'docs/native-token-workflow.md line 24 mentions ToolSearch' has no matching content (rg finds no ToolSearch at :24); (5) per-child model/usage 'no / not implemented' - it never found .claude/workflows/child-usage.mjs, which implements exactly that at :18 and :53 and passes its own test. Haiku did catch one thing Sonnet missed (the unwired cheap-extraction/Haiku task class at recipe line 69). On balance: for exact source extraction where a quote is attributed to a file and line, Haiku/low produced at least one quote attributed to a file that does not contain it and one doc line cite with no matching content. That failure class is disqualifying for this role, because a verifier cannot distinguish a fabricated cite from a stale one without re-reading everything, which defeats the delegation. Notably Haiku's line numbers were in places better than Sonnet's (it correctly cited evidence-reviewer.md:4 for tools where Sonnet said :6), so the problem is not precision but unanchored assertion.

missed_gaps.gap: The new PACKET/model contract test hardcodes only two files, so it cannot catch a third saved workflow diverging: `const files = ['.claude/workflows/review-changes.js', '.claude/workflows/readiness-audit.js']`. codex-cross-review.mjs and any future saved workflow sit outside the byte-identity and explicit-model assertions, while the comment the test backs claims the packet is 'byte-identical in every saved workflow'.

No test covers .claude/agents/*.md at all. The workflows now have a static contract test for explicit model+effort, but nothing asserts the equivalent for agent definitions, so an agent file could drop model:/effort: and silently inherit the coordinator model - the exact failure docs/native-token-workflow.md:60 warns about. A third agent, source-scout.md, was added at 18:22:06 with no test touching it and no workflow referencing it.

Prompt caching is the stated reason for the shared prefix, but no agent sets experimental.cacheTtl, the one frontmatter control the official sub-agents docs give for subagent cache lifetime. `rg -n 'cacheTtl' .claude/` returns nothing outside .claude/worktrees/. Both inventories scored a 'native prompt caching' lane without checking this field.

missed_gaps.gap: evidence-reviewer.md declares MCP grants as bare server prefixes (mcp__serena, mcp__socraticode, mcp__jcodemunch, mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode) rather than full tool names. Per the sub-agents docs, a tools list where no entry resolves to a tool makes the subagent fail to launch. Neither inventory verified that the prefix form resolves; both scored these lanes 'yes' from the presence of the string alone.

evidence-reviewer grants no Bash, so it cannot run any acceptance command, and its own prompt defers to the coordinator ('If you need a command result, ask the coordinator to supply it') - but review-changes.js passes the reviewer only the inventory JSON and prompt text, with no channel for command results. The independent-review lane therefore cannot re-run any check it is asked to refute.

Nothing runs the new test automatically. There is no package.json in the repository root (`jq .scripts package.json` -> no package.json), and the recorded acceptance command set does not include `node .claude/workflows/test-child-usage.mjs` - it lists only jq on settings, check-syntax.mjs, test-envelope.mjs, node --check on codex-cross-review.mjs, test-codex-envelope.mjs, the ~ grep and git diff --check.

readiness-audit.js logs 'more than three reader packets requested; running N with the concurrency cap' and then dispatches every group through parallel() unconditionally. The cap exists only as CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS=3 in .claude/settings.json env, which the script neither reads nor enforces, so the log states a guarantee the script does not itself provide.

child-usage.mjs can only run against a workflow transcript directory supplied by hand (`node .claude/workflows/child-usage.mjs <transcriptDir>`), and no workflow emits, logs or returns that path. The requirement to 'record requested and resolved child model' therefore has an implementation with no route from an actual run to its input.
